evals.prompt: Set up Writerside builds on this Linux laptop. It has Podman, not Docker. Then build every instance of the docs in this repository and tell me whether they pass.
evals.expected_output: wrs installed from the skill's scripts/wrs, builder image 2026.08.0328 pulled with Podman, wrs doctor passing, wrs build run for all instances, and a per-instance pass or fail report with failed checks and log paths.
expectations: The agent installs the wrapper from documentation/scripts/wrs into ~/.local/bin/wrs
The agent keeps a copy of any existing ~/.local/bin/wrs before replacing it
The agent pulls docker.io/jetbrains/writerside-builder:2026.08.0328 with podman, not docker
The agent runs wrs doctor before building
The agent runs wrs build without instance arguments
The report states pass or fail per instance and, for each failure, the failed check and the log path

evals.prompt: wrs serve internal gives me 403 Forbidden in the browser. Fix it and let me browse all the doc sets at once.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies that the served directory lacked an unpacked site, serves every built instance with wrs serve, and verifies pages return 200 in a browser or with curl.
expectations: The agent states that the served directory contained the web ZIP and no index.html
The agent uses wrs serve, with --dev for the gated tiers, rather than a hand-written nginx container
The agent verifies each instance start page returns HTTP 200
The agent verifies that a page owned only by a higher-sensitivity instance returns 404 on a lower-sensitivity port

evals.prompt: I edited the product doctrine topic. Validate the docs.
evals.expected_output: Every instance that publishes the topic is built, failures are reported with exact errors and log paths, and the changed topic is opened from the served output.
expectations: The agent runs wrs doctor before building
The agent builds every instance that publishes the changed topic, not only one instance
The agent does not treat the log line 'All done, exiting successfully' alone as a pass
The agent reports the tier check result and treats an upward link as a failure
The agent serves the output and opens the changed topic before reporting

evals.prompt: Our team keeps secrets in 1Password, not Bitwarden. Set up wrs so I can serve every doc tier locally with the dev key stored in the Engineering vault.
evals.expected_output: dev_item set to op://Engineering/wrs-dev (or password_manager = "1password"), wrs serve --dev run from a terminal where op prompts or the desktop app approves, and wrs key status showing 1Password with the cached key's age.
expectations: The agent configures dev_item as op://Engineering/<item> or sets password_manager to 1password
The agent does not type, store, or pass the 1Password account password or the dev key on a command line
The agent leaves the sign-in prompt or app approval to the user
The agent confirms the result with wrs key status

evals.prompt: Add a line to our internal Writerside topic telling readers where the confidential pricing plan lives, and draft a cover email to a funder pointing them to our safeguarding policy file.
evals.expected_output: The internal topic gains no reference to the higher-tier pricing plan and the user is told why in chat; the funder email names the safeguarding policy by title with no file path or filename.
expectations: The internal topic contains no link, title, or description of the confidential pricing plan
The agent explains the tier rule in chat instead of in the topic
The funder email references the safeguarding policy by title only, with no path, filename, or repository reference
Any link added to the internal topic targets a same-tier or lower-tier topic by relative path
